featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Adeshwari Biryani Center after seeing many Instagram reviews, and we specifically went to try their biryani and fried chicken.

There was around 30 minutes waiting, which felt a bit long, but it was understandable considering how popular the place is.

Talking about the seating, it is a bit congested, and you may have to share your table with others. However, luckily, we got a separate seat for two, which was nice and made us comfortable.

After that, we ordered fried chicken with kurcha paratha and chicken biryani, and to be honest, every dish was just perfect. Even with the rush, they did not compromise on taste at all, which was really impressive.

They also served Guntur-style parotta with curd and sides along with the biryani, and everything tasted really yummy.

Overall, it was a really good experience, and the food quality definitely made the wait worth it.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hi Janhavi,

Thank you so much for such a detailed and thoughtful review. We’re really glad you decided to visit us and try the biryani and fried chicken.

Happy to hear that you enjoyed the food and that everything lived up to your expectations, especially even during a busy time. That’s something we always aim for.

We understand your point about the waiting time and seating. It does get a bit tight during peak hours, and we truly appreciate your patience with that.

Your feedback means a lot to us, and we’re really happy that the overall experience made the wait worthwhile for you. Looking forward to welcoming you again soon!

Warm regards,
Aadeshwari Biryani Center Team

Really disappointed with the taste of Andhra Chicken Biryani & Chicken 65 Boneless.
Price is Rs. 340 For Chicken 65 Boneless Very expensive not worth for the price.
One of the worst thing is the waiting time. We have waited more than 1 hr to had our lunch. No comfortable seating.

featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:

We’re really sorry that your visit turned out to be disappointing, especially after travelling such a long distance to try our food. We completely understand how frustrating it must feel when expectations built through social media don’t match the experience.

Warm regards,
Aadeshwari Biryani Center Team

featured_reviews.name: Bhavya Bhat
featured_reviews.review_text:
Saw Aadeshwari Biryani Center all over reels and finally decided to give it a try, but honestly it was a huge let down. Tried their Andhra Special Biryani, Ardeshwari Fried Chicken, and Egg Parotha with curry. The biryani lacked the flavour I was expecting, the chicken was slightly chewy, and the fried chicken surprisingly lacked spice too. Even the cold drinks served weren’t cold enough.

Maybe it was just an off day, but for me it’s more of a one-time try. However the staff and servers were extremely polite and attentive, so kudos to them for that.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Thank you, Bhavya Bhat, for taking the time to share your detailed feedback about your experience at Aadeshwari Biryani Center. We truly appreciate your honest review and are glad to know that you found our staff and servers polite and attentive.

At the same time, we are sorry that the Andhra Special Biryani, fried chicken, and overall flavours did not fully meet your expectations during your visit. We also regret the inconvenience caused by the cold drinks not being served at the right temperature. Your feedback regarding flavour consistency, spice levels, and food texture has been noted carefully and will be reviewed with our kitchen team.

We value every customer experience and continuously work on improving our food quality while maintaining authentic Andhra-style flavours. We hope you will consider visiting us again in the future for a much better dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Dikshita
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had an amazing food experience at Aadeshwari Biryani Center 🤤

We ordered Fried Chicken, Andhra Biryani, and Thatte Idli with Chicken Sukka. every dish was packed with authentic South Indian flavours. The Andhra biryani had the perfect spicy kick and rich aroma, the fried chicken was crispy and juicy, and the thatte idli with chicken sukka was super soft paired with spicy, flavourful sukka… such a perfect combo!

Loved that they serve food on a banana leaf, which adds a traditional touch to the whole experience. They also provide raita and rasam with every dish, making the meal even more satisfying.

If you are a biryani & spicy food lover, this place is definitely a must try  Highly recommended for authentic taste 😋 👌

featured_reviews.name: Saqlain Sethia
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a true food lover, Noor Mohammadi Hotel is nothing short of heaven. I finally got to try their legendary Nalli Nihari, and honestly… it lives up to every bit of the hype.

The nihari was rich, slow-cooked to perfection, with the marrow melting into the gravy, bursting with deep, soulful flavors. Every spoon felt warm, comforting, and indulgent — the kind of dish that makes you pause and appreciate good food.

And just when I thought it couldn’t get better, the meal ended with their Rabdi. Thick, creamy, and perfectly balanced in sweetness, it was the ideal dessert to round off such a hearty feast. You can actually taste the patience and tradition in every bite.
No fancy plating, no unnecessary drama — just authentic, old-school flavors that hit straight to the heart. Noor Mohammadi doesn’t just serve food; it serves heritage on a plate.

featured_reviews.name: Shaikh Kadir
featured_reviews.review_text:
This place truly gave me a heartwarming experience and the kind of food that reminds you what real, honest cooking tastes like. It’s amazing to know that this restaurant has been around for over 102 years, carrying forward a legacy of authentic flavors and consistent quality. You can really feel that heritage in every dish they serve.

The food was absolutely delicious and clearly made with care and good-quality ingredients. I loved how every bite had that traditional touch — nothing fancy, just pure, flavorful food made right. My personal favorites were the Mutton Sanju Baba and the Haleem. The mutton was soft, juicy, and full of flavor, while the haleem was rich, creamy, and perfectly spiced — the kind that instantly makes you smile after the first spoonful.

The ambiance adds to the experience — simple, calm, and full of character. It feels like a place where stories have been shared for generations. The staff was really friendly and attentive, making sure we were comfortable and enjoying our food.

Overall, I’d say this isn’t just a restaurant it’s a part of culinary history. If you love traditional, soulful food that warms both your heart and your stomach, this place is a must-visit.

featured_reviews.name: Moumita Roy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Noor Mohammadi Hotel and it was a truly memorable experience for anyone who loves authentic Mughlai food. This place is quite iconic and well-known for its rich, flavorful dishes.

The highlight, of course, is their legendary chicken dishes—especially the Chicken Sanju Baba, which is packed with bold spices and has a rich, indulgent taste. The food overall is delicious, with generous portions and that proper old-school Mumbai Mughlai flavor.

The ambience is simple and no-frills, but that’s part of its charm. It’s more about the food than the setting. The place is usually quite crowded, and you might have to wait a bit for a table, especially during peak hours.

Service is quick considering the rush, though it can feel a bit hectic at times. Hygiene and seating are decent but not luxurious, so it’s best to go in with the right expectations.

Overall, Noor Mohammadi is a must-visit if you’re looking to enjoy authentic, hearty Mughlai cuisine in Mumbai. It’s not about fine dining, but about great taste and a truly local food experience.

featured_reviews.name: Faiz F
featured_reviews.review_text:
Once a legendary staple of Mumbai’s culinary scene since 1958, Gulshan-e-Iran appears to have lost the magic that built its heritage. The shift away from their famous buff seekh has left a noticeable void in the menu that the chicken alternatives simply cannot fill. A recent attempt at the Chicken Seekh Kabab and Tawa Paratha proved to be a major disappointment, lacking the flavor profile one expects from such an established name. While the Chicken Kheema in Green Masala offers a saving grace with its well-balanced, mild spices, the overall lack of variety in the tawa and grill sections forced a pivot to basic Dal Rice just to round out the meal.

Ultimately, this iconic spot now functions better as an emergency food option rather than a dining destination. Given its location in a high-traffic business market with limited surrounding choices, it serves its purpose for a quick, functional bite, but it no longer carries the "must-visit" status of its glory days. For those seeking a more satisfying meal in the area, Patel Restaurant stands out as the superior recommendation.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently dined at Jaffer Bhai - Mashid, an establishment conveniently located near the Crowford Market Junction on the way to Mohd Ali Road. Parking can be a bit of a gamble here, so you're on your own in that regard. The restaurant occupies the first floor, reserving the space below for the bustling kitchen.

The overall ambiance was quite pleasing, exuding a Middle Eastern vibe without going overboard on extravagance. The generous use of mirrors throughout the restaurant added a unique touch.

Now, let's get to the highlight - the food. While Jaffer Bhai is renowned for its Biryani, we decided to explore other options this time. We began with the Mughail, a delightful choice.

For starters, we savored the Chicken Boti Tikka, a medley of perfectly cooked chicken pieces marinated in their signature spices and charred on charcoal, elevating its flavor profile to extraordinary heights. This dish was served alongside a Coriander and Mint Chutney, creating a stellar combination that easily earns a perfect score.

Moving on to the main course, we ventured into the realm of Chicken Lahori Tawa. The gravy was an absolute revelation, captivating our taste buds from the very first bite. The boneless chicken pieces were incredibly tender, swimming in a creamy, impeccably cooked sauce. This dish was accompanied by Reshmi Roti and Rumali Roti, a pairing that seemed like a match made in culinary heaven.

Although we regrettably missed out on their famed Biryani, our taste buds were so thoroughly impressed by the food we did try that there's no doubt the Biryani would have been equally superb.

In addition to its culinary prowess, Jaffer Bhai's offerings are also kind on the pocket, making it an excellent choice for those seeking delicious fare without breaking the bank.

I'm already looking forward to my next visit, eager to explore their other delectable offerings, and of course, indulge in their renowned Biryani. This experience was one for the books!

featured_reviews.review_text:
As salaamu alaykum (peace be upon you) dear brothers and sisters, how are you all? You can now travel to Mumbai without any hesitation or fear of covid, which was anyways self created.

Today I’m writing about THIS famous eatery house called Delhi Darbar. It serves some typical Mughlai and Awadhi cuisine, and they are famous for their biryani. It’s pioneer owner Jafferbhai expired last year and may he rest in peace, amen.

We, the 3 Sayeds, visited this place a week back since my son Arsh wanted to dine there. This was after special Ramadaan namaaz at around midnight time, and fortunately for us, the restaurant was still open to serve us food.

We ordered Al Baik style fish fry served with Toum, the garlic dip. Delicious. Crispy. Al Baik is a chain of store in Saudi Arabia famous for their fish and chicken fries.

Then we had Mutton Khichda, which is a tedious blend of broken wheats and pulses, and then separately cooked mutton added to it, and then the entire thing is all cooked to perfection by adding fried onions and mint and lemon, and THE GHEE or clarified butter. Finger licking it is. You will enjoy this just by itself, although a person like me loves to eat it along with a tanduri naan or chapati. It’s a heavy and filling dish. Quantity was reasonably good.

And then came their most popular Mutton Biryani. Biryani tastes best when cooked on a slow DUM fire with mutton in it. Of course if you’re a health conscious person, or prefer to eat chicken rather than mutton, chicken biryani is also served here. Earlier they used to serve Dahi raita along with biryani, but not anymore. Everyone has gone commercial, so dahi kachumar raita has to be ordered separately. I wish they didn’t charge this separately and included it in the meal itself.

We finished it off with a soft drink to settle down  all that heavy food, but delicious no doubt.

YOU HAVE TO EAT HERE AT LEAST ONCE.

Tucked near the lively Crawford Market, this restaurant has carved a niche for itself among Mughlai food lovers, especially for late-night cravings. While the food is generally average, the menu features a few standout dishes that are truly unique and worth a try.

Compared to nearby favorites like Delhi Darbar and Persian Darbar, prices here lean on the higher side, but if you’re after some signature Mughlai flavors in a convenient central location, it’s worth the splurge.

Do note that the service can be quite slow and definitely needs improvement, so patience is key. There’s almost always a wait, particularly on weekends and late evenings. Plan ahead, come hungry, and make sure to sample their must-try specialties for a fulfilling experience. Perfect for those who enjoy rich, traditional Mughlai fare in a vibrant, bustling setting.

The service is top-notch and quick. The best part? They’re open till 4:30 AM, which is a blessing for late-night food lovers! Their menu is extensive with lots of variety to choose from. The interior is clean, comfortable, and fully air-conditioned, which is such a relief, especially in warm weather. The atmosphere inside is calm, welcoming, and well-maintained, making it a really nice place to sit and enjoy a relaxed meal.

The food was really good, with plenty of delicious options to choose from. Everything tasted fresh and well-prepared, and the menu has a great variety, so there’s something for everyone. A special shoutout to the papadam — it was absolutely delicious, perfectly crispy, light, and full of flavor. One of those simple items done so well that it really stands out!

Service was smooth and pleasant, and overall the experience felt comfortable and easy. It’s definitely one of those hidden gems that doesn’t look like much from the outside, but once you’re inside, you’re so glad you gave it a chance.

If you’re nearby, don’t judge this place by its exterior — walk in, sit down, and enjoy. Great food, clean space, air conditioning, and lots of tasty options. I would absolutely recommend and would happily return! ✨🍽️

Here we had the softest Kakori Kebabs that didn’t even require chewing - that’s how soft they were; this creamy Nalli Barra with Naan and smooth gravy; a Lebanese dish called Lamb Arayes that went very well with their Hummus and their legendary Chicken Yakhni Pulao. They don’t just do Indian food though - their Green Thai Curry with Sticky Rice is better than a lot of Asian restaurants. For desserts, they have a new menu from which you should definitely try the Tiramisu and Milk Cake. The next time you’re around Fort, you have to check out Ustaadi!

Cafe Madras is one of the most iconic South Indian restaurants in Mumbai and truly lives up to its reputation. Located in the heart of Matunga, this place is famous for serving authentic and delicious South Indian food with consistent quality for decades. The moment you enter, the aroma of fresh filter coffee, ghee, and spices creates a warm and nostalgic feeling.
I tried their famous dosa and idli, and both were excellent. The dosa was perfectly crispy with a flavorful potato filling, while the idli was soft, fresh, and served with tasty chutneys and sambhar. Their filter coffee was another highlight — strong, aromatic, and refreshing. Despite being crowded most of the time, the service is quick and efficient, which is impressive.
The restaurant maintains cleanliness and has a simple yet traditional atmosphere that adds to the experience. Prices are also reasonable considering the quality and popularity of the food. Overall, Cafe Madras is a must-visit place for anyone who loves authentic South Indian cuisine. It perfectly combines taste, tradition, and quality, making every visit memorable.

featured_reviews.name: ADITYA SALVI
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐ **DP’s Hotel – A Matunga Classic Opposite Ruia College** ⭐
📍 *Matunga East | Opposite Ruia College*

If you're anywhere near Matunga East and your cravings are leading you towards something delicious, flavorful, and comfortingly local – **DP's Hotel** is a name that *needs* to be on your radar. A long-time favorite among college students, families, and foodies alike, this spot has stood the test of time. I dropped by for a casual evening bite, and here’s the lowdown on my experience.

🍛 **FOOD REVIEW**:

🧈 **Pav Bhaji – 4.5/5**
Easily one of the best in town! Rich, buttery, and full of flavor, it strikes the right balance between spice and tanginess. Served hot with toasted pavs, this dish is a total crowd-pleaser. Definitely a must-try!

🍺 **Fruit Beer – 5/5**
An absolute nostalgic winner. Served chilled, this non-alcoholic classic is a throwback to simpler days. Fizzy, sweet, and perfectly refreshing – it complements the spicy food beautifully.

🍯 **Honey Chilli Plum Potato – 4/5**
A delightful fusion starter. Crispy potatoes tossed in a sticky sweet & spicy glaze, with a hint of plum that sets it apart. Would’ve loved it a tad spicier, but still very satisfying.

🍨 **Gadbad (Mangalore Special Dessert) – 3.5/5**
This colorful layered dessert has all the potential to be a star. However, mine I had whe  the ice cream partially melted – which unfortunately dulled the magic a bit. If you're ordering this, make sure it comes straight from the freezer. That said, the combination of fruits, jelly, nuts, and ice cream is still worth trying once!

🏠 **AMBIENCE & SERVICE**:

DP’s isn’t trying to be a fancy fine-dine, but it delivers big on cleanliness and comfort. The vibe is casual, with fast-moving service and staff that are polite and efficient. It’s the kind of place where you can chill with friends, binge on some desi snacks, and leave with a full heart (and fuller stomach).

✨ **PRO TIPS**:

* **Come early in the evening** to avoid the post-college crowd rush.
* **Grab a seat inside** for a more relaxed dining experience – outdoor seating can get a bit noisy.
* **Try their iconic milkshakes and dosas** if you’re coming back for round two – they’re tasty!

Overall, DP’s is a true **Matunga gem**. Consistent, value-for-money, and packed with flavor. Whether you're a first-timer in the area or a long-time local, this spot deserves a visit – and maybe even a second helping.

---

💬 **Rating: 4.3 / 5 overall**
Would definitely recommend for casual dining, snacking, or those nostalgic food runs with friends.

Udipi in Matunga truly stands out for serving one of the most authentic South Indian meals in the area. The food tastes homely, fresh, and full of flavour — from the perfectly crisp dosas to the soft idlis and that classic filter coffee which completes the meal beautifully.

What makes it even better is that the entire restaurant is fully air-conditioned, making dining here a pleasant experience even on hot days. The place is clean, well-maintained, and comfortable for families as well as groups of friends.

The service is quick, polite, and efficient — exactly what you’d expect from a traditional Udipi restaurant.

If you’re looking for genuine South Indian food in Matunga that combines great taste, comfort, and a welcoming vibe, this is definitely one of the best spots to visit. Highly recommended!

The Chicken Biryani was fragrant, well-balanced, and absolutely delicious. The rice was long-grained and perfectly cooked, each grain carrying the flavor of the spices without being oily or too heavy. The chicken pieces were juicy and generously portioned, blending beautifully with the biryani masala. It had that perfect mix of aroma, taste, and texture that makes you want another serving.

This hidden gem is lovingly run by a delightful sister-brother duo, whose passion for their native food shines through in every detail. The magic, however, truly begins in the kitchen, where their parents — the heart and soul of the place — cook each dish with pure love, warmth, and authenticity.

We indulged in their Saoji Mutton Thali, Saoji Chicken Thali, Chicken Biryani, and Mutton Biryani, and every dish told a story of rich tradition and bold flavor. The thalis are wonderfully wholesome — complete with generous servings of spicy, flavorful curries, soft chapatis, fragrant rice, comforting soup, refreshing chaas, a touch of sweetness in dessert, and their signature purnur — a unique vada meant to be savored with the Saoji gravy. It’s something you won’t find elsewhere, and it adds a truly authentic touch to the meal.

The biryanis, too, deserve a special mention — aromatic, full-bodied, and perfectly balanced, with every grain of rice infused with flavor. What’s even better is that you can ask to adjust the spice level according to your preference — from mild to authentically fiery.

What truly sets Nakod’s Biryani House apart is how genuine the entire experience feels — from the heartfelt hospitality to the unmistakable home-cooked essence of every bite. Whether you’re a fan of spicy Indian food or simply someone who loves exploring regional cuisines, this place will leave you curious, delighted, and craving more.
A must-visit for anyone who wants to discover the soulful and fiery world of Saoji cuisine!

featured_reviews.name: Kamlesh Gadilohar
featured_reviews.review_text:
1/5 – One of the Worst Mughlai Dining Experiences We've Had

We visited Delhi Darbar, Jogeshwari West for my brother's birthday celebration, expecting the quality and hospitality associated with the Delhi Darbar name. Unfortunately, it turned out to be one of the most disappointing dining experiences we've had.

We started with roasted and fried papad. The roasted papad had a small hair on it. I quietly removed it without informing my family to avoid spoiling the occasion, but such hygiene lapses should never happen.

For starters, we ordered the Shahi Kebab Platter, Mutton Kebab, and Finger Chips. The kebabs were the only items that tasted genuinely good, although the quantity was quite small. Even the Finger Chips portion was surprisingly small considering the pricing.

The rest of the food was disappointing:

Veg Crispy was overloaded with oil and had the smell of reused cooking oil. We hardly ate any of it and packed almost the entire dish. Nobody from the staff bothered to ask whether there was an issue.
Chicken Schezwan Tandoori seemed to be prepared using stale tandoori chicken.
Butter Chicken was very average and lacked the richness expected from a reputed Mughlai restaurant.
Mutton Masala was swimming in oil and had an ordinary taste.
Paneer Tikka Biryani contained hard paneer pieces, excessive oil, and very little flavor.
The Chicken Dum Biryani was the biggest disappointment. The rice quality was shockingly poor, consisting largely of broken "tukda" rice that we wouldn't even use for khichdi at home. It was excessively oily and filled with potato pieces. For a restaurant known for Mughlai cuisine, serving a biryani of this quality is simply unacceptable.

The service was equally disappointing. At one point, one of our family members had to get a plate himself because the attending manager was busy on a phone call. The manager came across as rude, inattentive, and unprofessional. Basic hospitality and customer service seemed completely missing.

What made the experience even more frustrating was that despite several dishes being left unfinished, no one from the staff showed any concern or made an effort to understand whether there was a problem with the food.

Our bill exceeded ₹5,000, yet the overall quality of food and service was nowhere near the level expected for that price. My family and I have dined at numerous Mughlai restaurants across Mumbai over the years, ranging from small establishments to premium dining venues, and this was honestly one of the worst experiences we've had.

A birthday celebration that should have been memorable for the right reasons ended up being memorable for all the wrong ones.

Poor food quality, excessive use of oil, questionable freshness, hygiene concerns, small portions, indifferent service, and premium pricing that simply doesn't match the experience. Based on this visit, I would not recommend Delhi Darbar, Jogeshwari West.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Dear Kamlesh,
It’s disheartening to learn about your recent visit and the shortcomings you experienced. The hygiene issue with the papad is particularly concerning, and I sincerely apologize for this lapse. We take cleanliness seriously and will investigate how this occurred. 
Thanks & Regards,
Jaffer Bhais Delhi Darbar

featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ A Complete Meal with the Perfect Sweet Ending!
This plate is a true celebration of flavors, from royal Awadhi kebabs to a classic dessert.
The Lucknow Gosht Galawati Kebab is the absolute star — incredibly soft, delicately spiced, and so tender that it melts in your mouth. Each bite reflects authentic Awadhi craftsmanship, rich yet perfectly balanced.
The Kafta (Kofta) Kebab is equally satisfying — juicy, flavorful, and cooked to perfection with a lovely outer crust and a moist, well-seasoned center. Paired with the light sautéed vegetables and the creamy baked cheesy side, the plate feels complete and thoughtfully curated.
To refresh the palate, the Big Cola (600 ml) does its job perfectly — chilled, fizzy, and refreshing.
And then comes the highlight of the ending — the Caramel Custard 🍮
Smooth, silky, and perfectly set, with just the right amount of caramel bitterness balancing the sweetness. It’s light, comforting, and an ideal way to close such a rich meal.
✔️ Authentic Awadhi taste
✔️ Excellent texture & balance
✔️ Well-presented, satisfying portions
✔️ Dessert that truly completes the experience
A meal that feels indulgent yet comforting from start to finish.
Highly recommended for kebab lovers and anyone who enjoys ending their meal on a sweet, classic note. 🌟🔥
